We used a social incentive delay task (SID)

description.value: A cued reaction time task in which participants responded to cues to view smiling male or female faces of varying intensity.

spans.text: In this cued reaction time task, cues are presented at the beginning of each trial indicating whether it is a reward trial or a control trial (see ).
Stimuli were presented in an event-related fashion.
Participants indicated their response by pressing the button of a fiber optic, custom-made, response box with the index finger of their right hand.

stimuli.value: Color photographs displaying smiling faces and graphical control stimuli.

spans.text: The stimulus material consisted of 66 color photographs displaying three different facial expressions of 22 professional actors (11 female, 11 male, NimStim set of Facial Expressions, ( )).

Reaction times and hit rates were assessed for all conditions and tested for differences in separate analyses of variance (ANOVA) with factors ‘smile intensity’, ‘sex of face’, and ‘sex of participant’.

presentation_software.value: Presentation (Neurobehavioral Systems, Inc.); operating system not reported.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to respond as fast as possible to all cue types, including control cues, by pressing a button when the target symbol appeared in order to obtain the anticipated smiling face on reward trials.
